chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man for whom the daytime prayers are missed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray them, if he so desires, after Maghrib, and if he so desires, after 'Isha'.
ai.seo_question: How to make up missed daytime prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of Qada (making up) missed daytime prayers by performing them after the evening prayers, offering flexibility between praying after Maghrib or after 'Isha. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that missed obligatory prayers can be compensated at any time, though it highlights the practical consideration of avoiding the time of Istishab (mid-afternoon) if one delays until after 'Isha. The narration underscores the leniency in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of make-up prayers, prioritizing the fulfillment of the obligation over strict temporal constraints.
